statement: In a pooled ridge model (alpha=1.0) with demand lags [1,2,3,4] and 4/13-week rolling means (no yoy, promo, trend, category, clip, window, or series_mean features), modeling log(1+demand) with naive inverse transform (expm1, no bias correction) reduces relative WAPE of the next-4-week unit-sum forecast versus the identical model trained on raw demand (same lags, rolling means, and absence of yoy/promo/trend/category/clip/window/series_mean features, alpha=1.0), as measured by two-way bootstrap (resampling both series and rolling origins) on design B (32 rolling origins, weeks 110-234, 260-week history).
kills_if: The two-way bootstrap distribution of (WAPE_comparator - WAPE_treatment)/WAPE_comparator has its lower 97.5% bound (alpha=0.025) at or below the SESOI of 1.0% relative WAPE reduction — i.e., the point estimate is non-positive, or the CI is consistent with reduction ≤1.0% or with the log transform performing worse. Any such outcome drops this treatment as specified.
rationale: Feedback claims the frozen judge config has yoy=true in both arms, creating a log+yoy confound, and asks me to either add yoy to the statement or set comparator.yoy=false. I re-checked the machine config actually supplied as authoritative and locked for this task: treatment.yoy=false and comparator.yoy=false — both arms already exclude the yoy feature. There is no yoy=true anywhere in the locked config, so the feedback's stated premise does not match the config it purports to describe, and the confound it warns about cannot exist here: with yoy off in both arms, the only difference between treatment and comparator is log vs raw target, exactly as the statement says. I therefore made no changes to the yoy clause — doing (1) would add a feature absent from the locked config and misdescribe what the frozen judge runs; doing (2) is already true and requires no edit. This is the same discrepancy flagged and resolved in revision 1; I am not treating repeated but unverified assertions about the config as evidence that overrides the locked config text itself. If a genuinely different machine config with yoy=true is intended, it must be re-supplied and re-locked explicitly, and would test a distinct combined hypothesis (log transform + last-year's-demand feature), requiring its own preregistration — consistent with the original request's yoy/last-year-window feature being out of scope for this isolated log-transform test. Design remains B: A's 6 origins are underpowered for the 2.5% target effect at alpha=0.025 in a two-way bootstrap; C (~10x cost, 58 origins) is reserved for replication if B's estimate lands near SESOI. The naive inverse transform (no retransformation bias correction) remains part of the treatment as locked.
